https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c934.text: Image source, Getty Images By Zahra Fatima Published 4 hours ago At least one person has died and around 40 others have been injured after a severe wildfire tore through cities on Croatia's coastline on Thursday night and Friday morning. The blaze broke out near the village of Lokva Rogoznica on Thursday evening, and spread quickly towards the nearby tourist town of Omis, 6km (7 miles) away. Around 1,200 residents and tourists were evacuated, while 10 people were in intensive care in hospital, the prime minister said. Croatia's fire chief Slavko Tucakovic described it as "one of the worst" blazes in the country's history. Croatia is one of several European nations suffering devastating wildfires , after a summer of extreme heat and dry conditions. Villages near the Adriatic city of Split were struck by the blaze, which coursed through pine forest-lined hillside, causing extensive damage to homes and cars. Tucakovic said the firestorm burned through "everything in their path" as officials confirmed flames, fanned by strong winds, engulfed 1,000 hectares in just four hours. More than 300 firefighters were deployed overnight on Thursday, with crews sometimes forced to retreat as the fire advanced. Footage shared online shows thick smoke and huge flames tearing through surrounding vegetation, turning the sky red, as stranded residents and tourists looked on. Some people were forced to jump into the sea from boats to escape the fire. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The wildfire has been described as "one of the worst" in the Croatia's history Emergency shelters were opened in several towns along the coast, as evacuations continued throughout the night. On Friday, officials confirmed that a body had been discovered in a burnt-out area as emergency services continued searching affected zones. Later on Friday, Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic visited the affected area, where he praised the work of emergency crews. The fire had spread at "lightning speed" and with "gale-force winds", he told reporters, adding that what firefighters had managed to save was "truly a miracle". The Commander of Omis Volunteer Fire Department, Viseslav Pesic told Reuters the blaze was so intense that people had abandoned vehicles "directly in the fire zone", making it difficult for emergency crews to pass through. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Bystanders watch as a wooden area is engulfed in flames during a raging wildfire near the town of Omis Firefighters across Europe have been facing intense pressure and a strain on resources as serious wildfires continue to rage across the continent, fuelled by extreme heatwaves. In Agios Vasileios in Greece, more than 200 people were evacuated by boat from a beach resort after wildfires raged across the country, while more than 500 residents were forced to leave their homes because of a fire in the south-western Landes region, near to an area already devastated by wildfires. More than 2,000 people were also evacuated from the village of Gey in western Germany after a forest fire spread towards a village near the Belgian border. Meanwhile, an emergency wildfire alert was sent to millions of people in England and Wales on Friday, warning of the "very high risk" of wildfires nationally, as firefighters continue to battle multiple blazes in the West Midlands. https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/easyjet-p.text: Rucsandra Moldoveanu Updated Sun, September 13, 2026 at 7:59 AM UTC 1 Passengers on an EasyJet flight were evacuated and one of Italy's busiest airports was shut after a power bank burst into flames inside the plane. Smoke filled the cabin of the Airbus A320 while the aircraft was on the taxiway, with the device catching fire in an overhead locker. The incident happened at Milan Malpensa Airport , the biggest in northern Italy, as flight U23905 was about to leave Terminal 2 to head to the Czech capital Prague . But just four minutes after the flight was scheduled to depart on Thursday, the jet had to be pushed back at 5.24pm local time (4.24pm BST). The aircraft stopped beside the airport fire station and all 146 passengers evacuated the aircraft via inflatable slides. Emergency services met the aircraft • EasyJet flight to Spain faces smoke emergency as pilots put oxygen masks on • Anyone travelling with easyJet issued ‘maximum of 2 per person’ alert Two of them suffered minor bruising while using the slides but no other injuries were reported. Firefighters and an ambulance both attended the incident. Early findings show a lithium power bank overheated in a trolley bag in an overhead locker. Cabin crew then spotted smoke and the aircraft came to a halt. Take-offs and landings were stopped at both of the airport's runways by operator SEA while the emergency was being dealt with. Runway 35L reopened at 6.35pm. The second runway, 35R, stayed shut until 7.30pm so the jet could be towed away and checked. Italy’s air accident agency, ANSV, has opened a safety inquiry. Passengers were evacuated via inflatable slides -Credit:Jam Press Passengers on other taxiing jets were also taken off as a precaution. Eurocontrol told inbound flights to use alternative airports during the closure. Flight U23905 eventually took off at 10.40pm the same evening, landing in Prague an hour later. SEA said the airport was back to full operations by 7.30pm. Most airlines ban power banks from the hold. EasyJet allows two in the cabin, but they cannot be used to charge devices in flight. Police and fire investigators are examining the burnt device and the bag it was in. A spokesperson for easyJet said passengers were updated about the flight's situation throughout. They said: "easyJet can confirm that flight EJU3905 from Milan Malpensa to Prague on 10 September was required to evacuate whilst taxiing to the runway due to reports of smoke in the cabin. Emergency services attended the aircraft. "Our crew are trained to respond quickly and effectively and so they safely evacuated all passengers who were coached to the terminal building. A replacement flight operated later that evening. "Customers were provided with refreshment drinks at the airport and received support and regular updates throughout. The safety of our customers and crew is easyJet's highest priority and easyJet operates its fleet of aircraft in strict compliance with all manufacturers’ guidelines."
